excerpt: qarunbook is a test-plan tool for web, Android and iOS apps that your team and your AI assistant can work through over MCP; a fixed bug waits for a retest. Plans, alternatives and launch Q&A.
content:
qarunbook (short for "QA runbook") is a tool for the testing people do by hand on a real build before a release. You write a test plan where every check has steps and an expected result, or have an AI assistant draft it from your app's code. Then you, your team or your AI assistant work through it, recording a pass or fail for each platform: web, Android and iOS.

Issues stay attached to the check that found them. When an issue is marked fixed, the check shows "retest" rather than "passed" until someone checks the new build again. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or any other MCP client can read what failed, record results and follow up on fixes, acting under your name and role. It connects to GitHub, GitLab, Linear, Jira, Slack, Teams, Sentry, PostHog and Zapier, and has a REST API on every plan. It does not run automated tests.

qarunbook is built by Ifeanyi Ejindu; the site says it is made by Skill Seeds. It launched on Product Hunt on 4 October 2026 and finished #36 for the day with 62 upvotes. Paid plans are a flat price per workspace rather than per seat.

We have not tested qarunbook ourselves. This page brings together its official site, pricing page and terms, its Product Hunt page and the official pricing pages of comparable tools, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.os: Browser; AI access through MCP (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and others)
profile.starts_at: Free plan; paid from $29/month per workspace
profile.summary_short: Test-plan tool for web and mobile apps that teams and AI assistants work through, with retests for fixes
use_cases: Running a pre-release test pass across web, Android and iOS
Making sure a bug marked fixed is actually re-checked on the new build
Letting an AI assistant draft the test plan from your code and record results over MCP
Assigning checks or whole platforms to specific testers
Tracking bugs after launch, with or without a check behind each one

paragraphs: Ifeanyi Ejindu says he has shipped a lot of apps, and every time, testing before a release turned into a job of its own: working out what to check, explaining how to check it and chasing bugs. The one that hurt most was a bug marked "fixed" that nobody looked at again on the new build.

qarunbook keeps that work in one place, he explained: a plan that says how to test, results per platform, issues that stay on the check that found them, and a "retest" state for fixes. He was clear that it doesn't run automated tests; it is for the testing that people and their AI assistants do on a real build. He asked teams that already have a test plan to import it and tell him where it didn't fit.
launch_story.attribution: Ifeanyi Ejindu, maker, on Product Hunt

fit: ship web or mobile apps and test them by hand before each release
use Claude Code, Cursor or Codex and want your assistant to work through the same test plan
have a team and dislike per-seat pricing: paid plans are flat per workspace
not_fit: want automated end-to-end tests run for you (qarunbook doesn't run them; tools like QA.tech or TestSprite do)
need more than one app or more than one person for free: the Free plan is 1 app, just you

pricing.intro: qarunbook charges a flat price per workspace, never per seat, in US dollars before tax. Paying yearly gives two months free.

plans.name: Free
plans.detail: 1 app, just you; 150 checks tested and 30 issues a month; 1 AI import a month; 2 GB storage; every integration, MCP, both AI skills and the API. No card

plans.name: Team
plans.detail: Unlimited testing, 15 apps, up to 15 members, 2 AI imports and 1 checklist from code a month, 50 GB storage, roles and join links

plans.name: Business
plans.detail: Unlimited testing and apps, up to 50 members, unlimited AI imports, 3 checklists from code a month, 250 GB storage

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.detail: Unlimited apps, members, AI imports and storage; invoiced billing

notes: A checklist drafted from your code costs $10 each on qarunbook's AI beyond the plan allowance, and is free when you run it on your own AI.
A check counts once a month, the first time it gets a pass or fail; retests never count. Going over a limit deletes nothing, it just blocks adding more.
Cancelling takes effect at the end of the paid period; partial periods aren't refunded except where the law requires it (terms).
At launch the maker described the free plan as 2 apps and 5 people; the pricing page now says 1 app, just you, and we use the pricing page.

alternatives.intro: Testiny is on Product Hunt's alternatives list; Qase and TestRail are established test-management tools we added. Prices come from each product's own pricing page, checked on 14 October 2026.

items.name: Testiny
items.what: Test-case management: cases, plans and runs
items.starts_at: Free for up to 3 users; paid from $18.50/user/month (see its pricing page for the billing cycle)
items.difference: Priced per seat, with a larger free team allowance. qarunbook is a flat price per workspace and built around retests and AI assistants.

items.name: Qase
items.what: Test management for manual and automated runs, with AI test generation and an MCP server
items.starts_at: Free plan; Teams $35/user/month billed yearly ($42 monthly)
items.difference: Per-seat pricing and integration with automated test results from CI.

items.name: TestRail
items.what: Long-established test case and run management for larger QA teams
items.difference: Enterprise features such as SSO, audit logs and an on-premises option, priced per seat, with a free trial rather than a free plan.

alternatives.more: Product Hunt also lists QApilot, TestMu AI, Testpine, QA.tech, TestSprite, DogQ and QA Sphere, most of which focus on automated or AI-run testing.

asked: Assigning specific tests to team members (yes, per check or for a whole section or platform)
Notes or evidence for each result (a pass note can now be added next to an issue)
Where the name comes from ("QA runbook" written as one word)
criticised: Tools that mark work as done too early, which the maker says the retest state is built to prevent

quotes.text: Is there a way to assign specific tests to different team members?
quotes.author: Khaild Naseem

quotes.text: Many tools mark things as done too early. Does qarunbook support notes or evidence for each test result?
quotes.author: Mikkel Larsen

pros: Flat per-workspace pricing, never per seat
A fixed issue isn't counted as passed until it's retested
Separate results for web, Android and iOS
AI assistants can work the plan over MCP, acting under your name and role
Wide integrations and a REST API on every plan, including Free
Going over a limit never deletes data
cons: Free plan is limited to one app and one person
AI-drafted checklists cost $10 each on qarunbook's AI beyond the allowance
Plan limits have changed since launch, so check the pricing page before you rely on them

x.none: We found no posts about qarunbook on X yet.

faq.a: There is a free plan for one person and one app, with 150 checks tested and 30 issues a month and every feature, no card needed. Team is $29 a month and Business $79 a month per workspace.
No. Its maker says it is for testing that people and their AI assistants do on a real build.

faq.q: Can I assign tests to specific people?
faq.a: Yes. The maker says you can assign any check to one or more people, who get an email and an in-app notice, or make someone owner of a whole section or platform. Anyone on the team can still test any check.

faq.q: Can testers leave notes or evidence?
faq.a: Yes. Next to "Add issue" under each check there is "Add pass note" for recording what you saw working, and you can attach screenshots and recordings.

faq.q: How does my AI assistant connect?
faq.a: Through qarunbook's MCP server with a workspace token. A plugin adds two skills: /test-checklist drafts a plan from your code and /qa-runbook works through it.
"QA runbook" written as one word: quality assurance plus runbook, the step-by-step guide a team follows.
